newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA tender decision seen in hours-radio.
newsitem.headline: CA tender decision seen in hours-radio.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima will decide in the next few hours whether to reopen a tender for Creditanstalt-Banverein to allow bidders to improve their offers, Austrian radio said on Friday.
No one at the finance ministry was immediately available for comment. Earlier a spokesman said it was unclear whether there would be an announcement before the weekend.
Bidders for the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary shares said they too were waiting for official word from the government.
Market leader Bank Austria is up against rival offers from a consortium led by insurer EA-Generali and entrepreneur Karl Wlaschek, an outsider.
Bank Austria has topped the bidding, putting up some 16 billion schillings for the state's stake that is worth around 14.3 billion schillings at current market prices.

Klima, a Social Democrat, has come under pressure from conservatives within the government to reject Bank Austria's bid on the grounds it would not be a genuine privatisation. The Social Democrat-run City of Vienna effectively controls Bank Austria. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
